description: Single-panel scatter plot with a fitted curve — no table cells are present in the supplied image, despite the figure_id and the caption label "Table 1 Fig. 1". The x-axis is labelled "True strain" with linear ticks at 0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25 and 0.3; the y-axis is labelled "Variation in elastic modulus δE=E/E0 [%]" with gridlines at 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100. All data are diamond markers: one filled blue diamond sits at (0, 100%), marking the undeformed reference, while roughly thirty open diamonds fall from about 95% at ε≈0.01 to about 75% at ε≈0.25–0.27, i.e. a monotonic, progressively saturating loss of modulus with true strain. A solid black curve is fitted through the open symbols; an annotation with an arrow pointing to the curve prints E = E0*(351ε² − 160ε + 93.8), the middle coefficient being only partially legible. No legend, error bars, or specimen labels appear anywhere in the panel. The figure demonstrates that prior plastic deformation causes an irreversible, strain-saturating reduction of the elastic modulus, well described by a quadratic fit in true strain.
measured_quantities: variation in elastic modulus δE = E/E0 (%)

observations.observation: The y-axis is labelled "Variation in elastic modulus δE=E/E0 [%]" and is gridded from 50 to 100 in steps of 10.
The x-axis is labelled "True strain" with tick marks at 0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25 and 0.3.
A single filled blue diamond marker lies exactly at 100% at zero true strain, representing the initial (undeformed) elastic modulus used as reference.

The open diamond data points decrease monotonically with increasing true strain, from roughly the mid-90s percent near ε ≈ 0.01 to about 75% near ε ≈ 0.25–0.27, where the decline levels off; no numeric data labels are printed on the points.

A solid black fitting curve is drawn through the open symbols, and an arrow from the annotation points to it, printed as E = E0*(351ε² − 160ε + 93.8); the coefficient of the linear term is only partially legible.
The panel contains no legend, no error bars and no specimen/condition labels; the only text is the axis labels, the tick numerals and the fitted equation.
The plotted abscissa is labelled "True strain", whereas the caption refers to "plastic strain"; the figure does not itself state a plastic-strain quantity.
The caption labels this item as "Table 1 Fig. 1" and states that the variation in elastic modulus was measured as a function of plastic strain using a precision extensometer [3].
The caption's reference to "Table 1" implies a specimen-condition table, but no table, rows or composition entries are visible in the supplied image.

The citing text states that specimens with several conditions as shown in Table 1 were employed for comparison, so the plotted points belong to multiple test conditions whose individual identities are not marked in the figure.
The citing text states that the tensile test was performed to confirm the effect of movable dislocations, which is the mechanism the modulus drop is attributed to.

subfigures.description: Scatter plot of elastic-modulus variation δE = E/E0 [%] versus true strain; one filled blue diamond at (0, 100%) and ~30 open diamonds descending from ~95% (ε≈0.01) to ~75% (ε≈0.25–0.27), with a solid black quadratic fit curve annotated E = E0*(351ε² − 160ε + 93.8).
